x: It was good to see Mark Sinclair run well in his first Junior C.C. race and to welcome Andrew North to Belgrave. We hope he will be chasing brother Dave in the next few years.

Special mention for: Jim Biesty a new member who turned in one of the fastest colts times of the day. Andrew North who looked really sharp in moving the boys team from 8th to 3rd. Michael Blackmore who claimed to be unfit.
Andrew North returned after sickness to make a late season improvement in form with good performances in league races, 2nd in the Club Championships and 1st in the Points Scheme.
Close behind John are Andy North and Mike Blackmore who have not competed as much as they would like due to 'O' level exams but still ran good times.
The needle matches between Andy North and Mike Blackmore now stand at 2 to 1 in Andy's favour. Particularly noteworthy was new member David Palmer's very fine run in the Youths' race.
The team of John Warren, Andy North, Mike Blackmore and Dave Paimer gained a fourth in the Herne Hill League, then a bronze at Collingwood followed by a second to Aldershot in the Surrey League.

We'd heard that Andy North was recovered from his back injury and that [illegible]e'd been running some good 1500ms but didn't know if he would handle the longer [illegible]illy course at Brockwell Park.
Derek Clack and Mike Nouch continue to improve and young Andy North made a welcome return after a back injury which has put him out for the last year.
Junior Andy North surprised a few of our established men and with hindsight his run was to be a pointer towards his subsequent rapid improvement.
Andy North had a tremendous run to finish in 54th spot also in the Junior race but alas with John Warren and Alister Horton injured there was no-one to back them up.

John Gladwin ran 3rd fastest of the day with Paul Richley 10th fastest and Oliver Foote(Continueing his return to fitness) was 12th fastest. 18 year old Andy North was very impressive as he forced himself around in an isolated position to return a time which staked a real claim to a 12 stage relay leg.
But for most the outstanding run was from Andy North, who,having shaken off a niggling injury which has dogged him for 3 years, has shown rapid progress.

It seems like only yesterday when the North Brothers were the mainstay of our Road Relay teams. With ex-National CC Champ-Gerry-, and ex-Inter Counties 3mile winner-Geoff- in the team we always had a head start.

Remember those promising Youths -Andy North and Michael Blackmore? We hear that Andy has been invited to Michael's wedding in January but as it clashes with the Surreys we will have to lay on some high speed transport if our top Junior is to make both events.
This was the first sign of Andy North's breakthrough. 1.T.Eglan (AFD) 24.38; 2.R.Vassal (Wav) 3.R.Peel (AFD) 25.37; ..... 9.A.North (Belgrave) 27.00. 64 Finished.
Andy North was easily the pick of the Bels. runners with his run of 25 minutes 27 seconds which clinched him 11th position and led the team to 5th place.

Andy North turned in a good performance and is beginning to make a few people sit up and take notice as too is Martin Lake. The race was notable for the number of top class second claim members running for other teams.

Without wishing to pre-empt our next Edition's full report - Oliver Foote won, John Gladwin was second, Mark Sinclair 6th, and Dave North 7th to give an all time record score of 16 points. Read also next time of super runs from Andy North and Francis Ward.
Andy North took over 16 seconds in the lead and ran 32 seconds faster than last year (he was in the 'B' team then) to hand over still 14 seconds clear.

Andy North proved fastest of the short leg runners with the amazing 53 year old Laurie O'Hara second best. On the long leg Oliver showed little sign of his previous days 10km p.b. while Mike Hayes again ran exceptionally well.

Those that stand out are the two club records that were set; Andy North's junior 5,000 record of 14:55:8 at Battersea on 25th May and Glynn Tieoran's 1500 youth record of 4:02:8 also at Battersea on 3rd August.

Andy North seen here representing Surrey in the Junior Inter Counties broke through last winter to finish a highly respectable 20th in the Junior National C.C.Champs and put his excellent winters background to good use by breaking the Club's long standing Junior 5000m record with a fine 14.55.

Like the Curate's egg the Cross Country season was good in parts, initially promising a lot with a win in the South of Thames Junior, but turning out to be a lame effort with only Oliver Foote in the Seniors and Andy North in the Juniors showing impressive improvements with high placings in the National CC Champs.
Oliver Foote was on schedule to lead the individual championship but was on holiday for the last match. Notable improvements from Andy North, Martin Lake and Francis Ward.

Although the 5½ mile course was wet the stoney paths helped the faster track men to a good start and after 2 miles the 250 strong field was led by 4 Belgravians - Oliver Foote, Mark Sinclair, John Gladwin and Dave North, with Andy North and Francis Ward not far behind.

In the Juniors Andy North almost ran up to the form he had displayed in the Surrey league as he finished 5th to get a Surrey vest. Again the Juniors got 4th team and with a bit of luck could have got Silver.
In the Junior race Andy North proved he should have had a Surrey medal as he finished in 55th place with 33.27 to be the second Surrey Junior man home.
In the Juniors Andy North beat Surrey Junior Silver and Bronze medallists to continue his steady improvement. Seniors: 1.N.Braun 2.R.Treadwell 3.A.Bristow.

And as for the Juniors - what can you say of Andy North's run. While others sank to their knees Andy floated across the mud and reminded many of us who were fortunate to see his run of another great North of some 30 years earlier!
Andy North took the race by the scruff of the neck from the gun and would have created a record on Hughie Green's Clapometer at the finish line.

It was then a case of its and bits, Andy North, third Bels man home was struggling and we could tell by the look on his face that he was not happy with his own and knowing Andy he will be seeking revenge in the Southern and National.
Andy North · Sep 86
Among some of his squad during this period were Andrew North, Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin, who claims his first run for Belgrave was with Brian.
